draft.title: Exact values
card: Half a square with side 1 has angles 45°, 45° and 90°. By Pythagoras the hypotenuse is √2. So sin 45° = 1/√2, cos 45° = 1/√2 and tan 45° = 1.
Half an equilateral triangle with side 2 has angles 30°, 60° and 90°. Its short side is 1 and its other side is √3, by Pythagoras.
Opposite 30° is 1, so sin 30° = 1/2, cos 30° = √3/2 and tan 30° = 1/√3. Opposite 60° is √3, so sin 60° = √3/2, cos 60° = 1/2 and tan 60° = √3.
Leave answers as surds, not decimals. Example: sin 60° × cos 30° = (√3/2) × (√3/2) = 3/4.
draft.remember: Draw the special triangle, then read the ratio from its sides.

a.q: What is the exact value of cos 60°?
a.why: In the 30°, 60° and 90° triangle, the side next to 60° is 1 and the hypotenuse is 2, so cos 60° = 1/2. The value √3/2 is tempting, but that is sin 60° and cos 30°.
a.clue: Which side is next to the 60° angle?

b.q: What is the exact value of sin 30° + tan 45°?
b.why: sin 30° = 1/2 and tan 45° = 1, so the sum is 1/2 + 1 = 3/2. The option 1/2 is tempting, but it leaves out the tan 45° term.
b.clue: Find each value from its triangle, then add.
